# Was Spotify hacked?

**Not established.** No source we read says the Nov 24 outage was an attack, and none rules one out. Spotify has not given a cause. Outlets said the wrong-password errors did not by themselves mean accounts were hacked.

Incident: Spotify login outage, Nov 24 2026. Also reported as the Spotify outage, Spotify down and Spotify logged me out. First published Nov 24, 2026; last updated Nov 24, 2026, 10:45 AM ET.

Picture: The Spotify app playing music on a smartphone (resized). Not taken during this outage. Image: Unsplash, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Spotify_on_smartphone_(Unsplash).jpg).

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Spotify, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 24, 2026, 10:45 AM ET: **Spotify was back up for most users by about 7:15 AM ET on Nov 24. It still has not given a cause, and nobody has reported a hack.** Hourly check. Added 6 sources: Spotify's two status posts on X (Tier 4), and Reuters (via Khaleej Times), Tom's Guide, Android Authority and TechPulse (Tier 2). Label change: c005 (recovery) Reported to Confirmed, now reported independently by TechRadar, Reuters and Tom's Guide; q003 answered Confirmed; service set to back. New c009 (Reported): two outlets said the wrong-password errors did not by themselves mean accounts were hacked. c004 and t003/t005 now carry the posts' own times (6:56 and 7:08 AM ET); new t006. c008 widened to 5:30-6:34 AM ET. No cause, no attack claim and no denial found; main answer stays Not established. Staleness and privacy checks done.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Spotify users in at least a dozen countries reported login problems, with more than 16,500 Downdetector reports in the US alone. Spotify has not said how many people were affected.
- Who is affected: Spotify users on the morning of Nov 24 (US time) who were logged out and could not sign back in. Sign-ins were working again for most by about 7:15 AM ET. Users still having trouble can contact Spotify support.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 16,500+ | US Downdetector reports | Plus 8,000+ in the UK, per TechRadar |
| ~6:15 AM ET | Problems began | Other outlets say 5:30-6:34 AM ET |
| ~7:15 AM ET | Sign-ins working again | Per TechRadar; Spotify gave no end time |

### Known so far

- On the morning of Nov 24, many Spotify users were logged out and could not sign back in.
- Spotify's status account said it was aware of issues and checking them out. It gave no cause.
- Sign-ins were working again for most users by about 7:15 AM ET, about an hour after problems began.

### Not known yet

- What caused the outage. Spotify has not said.
- Whether it was a cyberattack. No one has claimed one, reported one, or ruled one out.
- How many people were affected.
- Exactly when the problem was fully fixed. Spotify has not given an end time, and some users reported trouble after its all-clear.

We looked for these and did not find them as of our check at 10:45 AM ET on Nov 24.

- A Spotify statement, blog post or status-page note giving the cause of the outage.
- A Spotify statement that the problem is fully fixed, with an end time. Its last post, at 7:08 AM ET, says only that things look much better.
- Any claim of responsibility, DDoS claim or credible report of a hack, or any statement ruling one out.
- Any cloud, network or sign-in provider's status page linking an outage to Spotify's.
- A count of affected users. Downdetector figures are user reports, not users.
- Downdetector itself. We relied on how news outlets relay it.
- An official Spotify status page we could rely on. One page that looks like a Spotify status page appears to be an unofficial template, so we do not cite it.
- Any link between this outage and other outages this month.

Added 6 sources: Spotify's two status posts on X (Tier 4), and Reuters (via Khaleej Times), Tom's Guide, Android Authority and TechPulse (Tier 2). Label change: c005 (recovery) Reported to Confirmed, now reported independently by TechRadar, Reuters and Tom's Guide; q003 answered Confirmed; service set to back. New c009 (Reported): two outlets said the wrong-password errors did not by themselves mean accounts were hacked. c004 and t003/t005 now carry the posts' own times (6:56 and 7:08 AM ET); new t006. c008 widened to 5:30-6:34 AM ET. No cause, no attack claim and no denial found; main answer stays Not established. Staleness and privacy checks done. | Label change |

Spotify has not given a cause, and nobody has reported a hack.** First draft. 5 sources (all Tier 2), 8 claims (2 Confirmed, 4 Reported, 2 Not established), 4 questions.
